skill.name: global-coding-style
skill.description: Maintain consistent code formatting, naming conventions, type safety, and automated code quality standards across PHP and TypeScript/JavaScript. Use this skill when writing or editing any PHP files (.php), TypeScript/JavaScript files (.ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx), when implementing type declarations and return types, when running code formatters (Laravel Pint, Ultracite) or linters, when running static analysis tools (Larastan), when naming variables, functions, classes, or files, when applying DRY principles, when removing dead code, or when preparing code for review or commit.
skill.summary: Guide PHP and TypeScript coding standards for formatting, naming, type safety, and review cleanup.
skill.author: DevanB

security_audit.summary: The static path traversal finding is confirmed because the skill directs the agent to read a parent-directory file outside the skill package. No evidence found of prompt injection, network access, command execution, or secret exfiltration in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle the standards document inside the skill package or replace the link with inline guidance reviewed as part of the skill.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read ../../../agent-os/standards/global/coding-style.md, which escapes the skill directory. This can cause filesystem reads of unreviewed project content outside the packaged skill.

high_findings.title: Path traversal sequence
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read ../../../agent-os/standards/global/coding-style.md, which escapes the skill directory. This can cause filesystem reads of unreviewed project content outside the packaged skill.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent style slows reviews and hides defects. This skill guides PHP and TypeScript work with formatting, type safety, naming, and cleanup rules.
actual_capabilities: Guides edits for PHP, TypeScript, JavaScript, TSX, and JSX files.
Promotes explicit PHP return types and parameter type hints.
Encourages TypeScript type usage in frontend code.
References Laravel Pint, Ultracite, Larastan, Lefthook, and CodeRabbit workflows.
Supports cleanup of unused imports, dead code, commented blocks, and duplicated logic.
limitations: Does not include executable formatter scripts or configuration files.
Requires project tools to be installed before formatter or analysis commands can run.
Focuses on PHP and TypeScript or JavaScript, not other languages.
References an external standards document that is not bundled in the skill package.

use_cases.title: Prepare PHP Changes
use_cases.description: Apply return types, parameter hints, Laravel Pint formatting, and Larastan checks before review.

use_cases.title: Clean Frontend Code
use_cases.description: Review TypeScript or JavaScript changes for stronger types, consistent names, and Ultracite formatting.

use_cases.title: Review Mixed Stack Work
use_cases.description: Check PHP and frontend edits for dead code, duplication, and naming consistency before commit.

prompt_templates.title: Format Changed Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my changed PHP and TypeScript files using the global coding style. Apply available formatters and summarize any manual fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Type Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the current feature for missing PHP return types, parameter type hints, and weak TypeScript types. Fix issues that match the standards.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare For Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Clean unused imports, dead code, commented blocks, and duplicated logic in this branch. Run available quality tools and report remaining concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor To Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor the selected module for readability, naming consistency, DRY structure, and project style. Preserve behavior and explain each important change.

output_examples.input: Review a Laravel service before pull request review.
output_examples.output: Added explicit return types, removed unused imports, aligned names with project style, and reported that Larastan still needs one model annotation.

output_examples.input: Clean a TypeScript component after feature work.
output_examples.output: Replaced loose types, removed dead state, applied formatter guidance, and listed one naming issue that needs product confirmation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a mixed PHP and frontend branch for commit.
output_examples.output: Ran available style checks, removed duplicated logic, cleared commented code, and summarized remaining tool failures with next actions.

best_practices: Run the project formatter before requesting a final review.
Ask for behavior-preserving edits when applying style cleanup.
Use the skill with changed files or a specific module for focused results.
anti_patterns: Using the skill as a replacement for tests or static analysis.
Applying broad refactors without a clear review target.
Assuming referenced project tools are installed in every repository.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers PHP, TypeScript, JavaScript, TSX, and JSX files.

faq.question: Does it run Laravel Pint or Ultracite automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide use of those tools when they are available in the project.

faq.question: Can it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It supports style and quality checks before human or automated review.

faq.question: Does it include the full standards document?
faq.answer: No. The current package links to an external standards file instead of bundling it.

faq.question: Can it help remove dead code?
faq.answer: Yes. It explicitly covers unused imports, dead code, and commented-out blocks.

faq.question: Is it useful for pre-commit workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It references Lefthook and quality checks for commit preparation.
